collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Someone has moved the stone between two gardens: accuse the neighbor, or ask the elders to measure.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The boundary stone between (subject)'s garden and (friend)'s has moved a full stride into (subject)'s garden overnight. (subject) is sure (friend) did it. (friend) swears (friend.he/she) did not. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) accuses (friend) at the gathering. (friend) is furious. The argument goes on until an elder points out the pig tracks around the stone. The pigs moved it, rooting for grubs. (subject) has to apologize. It is very awkward.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The elders come with a rope and the old marks, and measure. They put the stone back. They also find pig tracks. Nobody accuses anyone. (subject) and (friend) build a little fence together, against the pigs.
